correctness.rationale: If \(P\ge5\) is the largest generator prime, no numerator \(r+1\) from a smaller prime \(r\) can be divisible by \(P\), because that would force \(r=P-1\), an even composite integer. Thus \(\nu_P(q)=-a_P<0\), while all prime factors introduced by \(P+1\) are smaller than \(P\). This makes the peeling step forced and strictly descending. At the terminal support \(\{2,3\}\), solving \(x=-u+2v,\ y=u-v\) gives the necessary and sufficient conditions \(u=x+2y\ge0,\ v=x+y\ge0\). Reversing the forced steps proves sufficiency and uniqueness. The packaged verifier replays all \(6560\) bounded exponent vectors on eight primes, all integers through \(20000\), and a reduced-rational grid.

originality.rationale: The focal paper states uniqueness of an already existing product representation but explicitly asks in Question 32 which rationals are representable. The new theorem converts the uniqueness mechanism into a complete membership and reconstruction algorithm, including an explicit terminal cone and the exact integer corollary. Targeted published-finding corpus, web, and OEIS searches did not locate an implication-equivalent criterion.
residual_risks: An unindexed note may have observed the same largest-prime peeling after the 2023 question.
The argument is elementary and short once the correct maximal-prime invariant is isolated, increasing the chance of an unpublished observation.
No asymptotic information about the density or height distribution of the rational semigroup is claimed.

value.rationale: The theorem directly answers a named open question from the focal paper with a finite recognition and reconstruction algorithm, rather than a special case or bounded computation. It also gives the clean structural corollary that the representable positive integers are exactly the \(3\)-smooth integers. The largest-prime descent is reusable for studying semigroups generated by rational local factors with triangular prime support.
